title: The January Finance Trap: Why Applications Submitted Now Take Longer to Approve
linkedin:
Most business owners think their finance application moves at the same pace year round.

It doesn't, and the gap shows up at exactly the wrong time.

Credit committees that meet weekly in winter often meet fortnightly, or not at all, through late December and into January. The relationship manager is still responsive. The committee behind them, the valuation panel if security is involved, the external verification steps, are all running on reduced summer staffing.

The result: an application that would clear in one to two weeks in April can sit for three or four weeks over the Christmas and New Year period. Not because anything is wrong with it. Because fewer people are available to look at it.

This catches owners every single year, usually the ones financing Christmas stock or extra wages right now, or planning to fund January and February growth off the back of a strong December.

The fix isn't complicated. Treat the application timeline as six to eight weeks through this period, not the two or three a lender might quote in winter. Lodge in late November for funds needed before the end of January, not in the second week of January itself.

For a bigger raise, equity, mezzanine, acquisition finance, the same slowdown compounds against an already long due diligence process.

Full piece on the ProfitPulse blog.

For business owners across Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria thinking about finance needs for January, there's a timing detail worth knowing before you apply.

Banks and lenders keep operating over the Christmas and New Year period, but the people who assess and approve credit take leave like everyone else. Credit committees that normally meet weekly often meet fortnightly, or not at all, through late December and into January. An application that would usually clear in one to two weeks can sit for three or four weeks over the same period, simply because fewer people are reviewing the queue.

This affects more than a simple facility top up. Behind the relationship manager sits a credit committee, sometimes a valuation panel, and often an external verification step, each running on its own reduced summer roster.

The practical response is to treat the application timeline as six to eight weeks through this period rather than the two or three a lender might normally quote, and to lodge now rather than waiting until the need becomes immediate in January.
